title.en: What you can wear, and your title

summary.th: นักศึกษาแต่งชุดไปรเวทหรือเครื่องแบบนักศึกษาตามเพศวิถีของตนได้ และไม่มีการบังคับใช้คำนำหน้านามที่แสดงถึงเพศ เว้นแต่กฎหมายกำหนด
summary.en: You may wear plain clothes, or the student uniform of your own gender identity, and no gendered title is imposed on you unless the law requires one.

userNeed: As a student, I need to know what I may wear and which title I am addressed by, so that I can attend class, exams and ceremonies as myself.

content.text: What you can wear
You may wear plain clothes on ordinary occasions, including in class and in exams, as long as it does not disturb other people's concentration or rights.
You may wear the student uniform of your own gender identity on ordinary occasions, at ceremonies, and at faculty events: for class, exams, placements, or dealing with any university office.
You may be photographed in the student uniform of your own gender identity.
Graduands may dress, and submit their gown photograph, according to their own gender identity.
Your title

No gendered title is imposed on students in any university process, except where the law requires one or where it is genuinely necessary, such as new student registration. No title appears on the student ID card.
If this is not respected
No contact for this is published. You can
report a problem
and you will get a reference.

The Student Union (TUSU), Tha Prachan

The Union is the executive body at Thammasat Tha Prachan. It allocates budget to clubs and independent groups, runs university-wide activities, operates student welfare services, and represents students to university executives. Established in 1952.
Union links:

The Student Council (TUSC), Tha Prachan
The Council is the legislative and scrutiny body. It drafts and approves rules on student activities, scrutinises the Union's decisions, policies and budget, and publishes
open data
. Established in 1970.
Both bodies work under the
regulation on student activities, B.E. 2563 (2020)
. To see whether the Union is keeping its promises, see
policy progress
